results.title: Eakin–Nagata theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an $A$-module. If the structure map $A \to B$ is injective and $B$ is Noetherian, then $A$ is Noetherian.

results.title: Faithfully flat algebras inside a localization equal the base ring
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A faithfully flat `R`-algebra `S` which embeds compatibly in a localization `K` of `R` has bijective structure map. No restriction on the denominators or domain assumptions on the rings are required.

results.title: Finite projective modules of fiberwise rank one are invertible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A finite projective module whose base change to every field has rank one is invertible.

results.title: Kaplansky's theorem on projective modules over local rings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every projective module over a commutative local ring is free.

results.title: Quillen–Suslin theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field and let $n$ be a natural number. Every finitely generated projective module over the polynomial ring $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ variables is free.

results.title: The sequence space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For $\mathbb{K}$ equal to $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, this is the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, with the norm $\|x\| = \left(\sum_{n} |x(n)|^2\right)^{1/2}$.

results.title: Cesàro means of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th Cesàro mean of $x$ is the average of its first $n + 1$ terms, $\frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k)$.

results.title: The Cesàro denominator $n + 1$ is nonzero
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $n$, the element $n + 1$ of $\mathbb{K}$ is nonzero.

results.title: Norm of the Cesàro denominator
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $n$, the element $n + 1$ of $\mathbb{K}$ (the denominator of the $n$-th Cesàro mean) has norm equal to the real number $n + 1$.

results.title: A Cesàro mean is bounded by the mean of the norms
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be any sequence and let $n$ be a natural number. Then $\|\frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k\| \le \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \|x_k\|$.

results.title: Cesàro means of square-summable sequences are square-summable
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the Cesàro means $\sigma_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$ satisfy: the series $\sum_n |\sigma_n|^2$ converges.

results.title: Cesàro means preserve square-summability
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, then the sequence of its Cesàro means $n \mapsto \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k$ also lies in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $C$ from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself that sends a sequence $x$ to its sequence of Cesàro means, $(Cx)(n) = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k)$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator is bounded by 2
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, viewed as a linear map, given by $(Cx)_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, $\|Cx\| \le 2 \|x\|$.

results.title: Cesàro operator on square-summable sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ is the continuous linear map from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself that sends a sequence $x$ to its sequence of averages, $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$. It is obtained from the Cesàro linear map with the bound $\|Cx\| \le 2 \|x\|$.

results.title: Formula for the Cesàro operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $(Cx)_n = \bigl(\sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k\bigr)/(n + 1)$.

results.title: Partial sums from Cesàro means
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k) = (n+1)\,(Cx)(n)$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator agrees with the Cesàro linear map
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the Cesàro operator, as a continuous linear map on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, takes the same value at $x$ as the Cesàro linear map, the same averaging map considered only as a linear map.

results.title: The Cesàro operator has norm at most 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k$, has operator norm $\|C\| \le 2$.

results.title: The first standard basis vector of $\ell^2$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The vector $e_0 \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the sequence with $e_0(0) = 1$ and $e_0(n) = 0$ for every $n \ge 1$.

results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $e_0 \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ be the first standard basis vector. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $e_0(n) = 1$ if $n = 0$ and $e_0(n) = 0$ otherwise.

results.title: The first basis vector is a unit vector
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The first standard basis vector $e_0 = (1, 0, 0, \dots)$ of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has norm $\|e_0\| = 1$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator has norm at least one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, has operator norm $\|C\| \ge 1$.

results.title: One step of inverting the Cesàro operator
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $x(n+1) = (n+2)\,(Cx)(n+1) - (n+1)\,(Cx)(n)$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, is injective.

results.title: The alternating harmonic sequence in $\ell^2$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The sequence $y$ with $y(n) = (-1)^n / (n + 1)$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ is square-summable, and it is regarded as an element of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: Coordinates of the alternating harmonic sequence in $\ell^2$
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $y$ be the alternating harmonic sequence, viewed as an element of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $y(n) = (-1)^n / (n + 1)$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator is not surjective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The sequence $y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ with $y_n = (-1)^n/(n + 1)$ is not in the range of the Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$. In particular $C$ is not surjective.

results.title: The Cesàro operator on standard basis vectors
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $e_n$ be the standard basis vector with $1$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ elsewhere. For all $n, k \in \mathbb{N}$, $(C e_n)_k = 1/(k + 1)$ if $n \le k$, and $(C e_n)_k = 0$ if $k < n$.

results.title: Adjoint of the Cesàro operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$. For every $y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the adjoint $C^*$ of $C$ satisfies

results.title: The adjoint of the Cesàro operator fixes the first basis vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0 = (1, 0, 0, \dots)$ be the first standard basis vector. Then $C^* e_0 = e_0$, where $C^*$ is the adjoint of $C$.

results.title: Second coordinate of the Cesàro operator at the first basis vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0 = (1, 0, 0, \dots)$ be the first standard basis vector. With coordinates indexed from $0$, $(C e_0)_1 = 1/2$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator is not self-adjoint
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, is not self-adjoint.

results.title: Cesàro test vectors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For a natural number $N$, the test vector $t_N = \sum_{i < N} \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} e_i$ has coordinate $1/\sqrt{N}$ at each $j < N$ and $0$ at each $j \ge N$; in particular $t_0 = 0$.

results.title: Coordinates of the Cesàro test vectors
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $N$ and $j$ be natural numbers. The $j$-th coordinate of the Cesàro test vector $t_N \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is $1/\sqrt{N}$ if $j < N$, and $0$ if $j \ge N$.

results.title: Norm of the Cesàro test-vector coefficient
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $N$, the norm of $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$, computed in $\mathbb{K}$, equals the real number $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$; for $N = 0$ both sides are $0$, with the convention $0^{-1} = 0$.

results.title: The Cesàro test vectors are unit vectors
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $N \ge 1$, the test vector $t_N \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, equal to $1/\sqrt{N}$ at the coordinates $0, \dots, N - 1$ and to $0$ elsewhere, has norm $\|t_N\| = 1$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator on a test vector, within its support
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ let $t_N$ be the test vector whose first $N$ coordinates equal $1/\sqrt{N}$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. For all $n, N \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n < N$, $(C t_N)_n = 1/\sqrt{N}$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator on a test vector, past its support
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ let $t_N$ be the test vector whose first $N$ coordinates equal $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. For all $N, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $N \le n$, $(C t_N)_n = N (\sqrt{N})^{-1}/(n + 1)$, where $(\sqrt{0})^{-1}$ is read as $0$.

results.title: Lower bound for the Cesàro operator on the test vectors
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $t_N$ be the $N$-th Cesàro test vector. For every natural number $N \ge 1$, $\|C t_N\|^2 \ge 5/4$.

results.title: The Cesàro images of the test vectors tend to zero coordinatewise
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, and for $N \ge 1$ let $t_N$ be the vector equal to $1/\sqrt{N}$ at the coordinates $0, \dots, N - 1$ and to $0$ elsewhere. Then for every fixed coordinate $n$, $(C t_{N+1})_n \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$.

results.title: The Cesàro operator is not compact
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The Cesàro operator $C$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(Cx)_n = (x_0 + x_1 + \dots + x_n)/(n + 1)$, is not a compact operator.

results.title: Digit of the N-expansion map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and $\alpha$ a real number, and write $I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$. The digit of a real number $x$ is $d(x) = \lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$, except that when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer, the digit of $\alpha$ itself is $d(\alpha) = N/\alpha - \alpha - 1$.

results.title: The $N$-expansion map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $N$ and a real number $\alpha$, the $N$-expansion map is $T_\alpha(x) = N/x - d_\alpha(x)$ for real $x$, where $d_\alpha(x)$ is the $N$-expansion digit: $d_\alpha(x) = \lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$, except that $d_\alpha(\alpha) = \lfloor N/\alpha - \alpha \rfloor - 1$ when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer. The map is meant to act on the interval $I_\alpha = [\alpha, \alpha + 1]$, but it is…

results.title: The digit away from the left endpoint
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be real numbers with $x \ne \alpha$. Then the digit of $x$ for the $N$-expansion map on $[\alpha, \alpha + 1]$ is $\lfloor N/x - \alpha \rfloor$.

results.title: The N-expansion map away from the left endpoint
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be real numbers with $x \ne \alpha$. Then the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha \le T_\alpha(x) < \alpha + 1$.

results.title: The left endpoint goes to the right endpoint when $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be a natural number and $\alpha$ a real number such that $N/\alpha - \alpha$ is an integer, with the convention $N/0 = 0$. Then the $N$-expansion map $T_\alpha$ satisfies $T_\alpha(\alpha) = \alpha + 1$.

results.title: Length of the ideal period words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the digit string of the ideal period word $d_n$ (the concatenation of its blocks of partial quotients) has length $|d_n| = 2^{n+1} - (-1)^n$.

results.title: Block counts of the ideal period words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the ideal period word $d_n$ contains exactly $2^{n-1}$ blocks $2, 2$, and the number $c_n$ of its blocks $2, 1, 1$ satisfies $3 c_n = 2^n - (-1)^n$; that is, $c_n = (2^n + 1)/3$ for odd $n$ and $c_n = (2^n - 1)/3$ for even $n$.

results.title: The marginal of probabilistic PCA and factor analysis is Gaussian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Z$ and $E$ be independent random vectors on a probability space, with values in $\mathbb{R}^q$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $Z$ has the standard Gaussian law $N(0, I_q)$ and $E$ has law $N(0, \Psi)$ for a positive semidefinite real $d \times d$ matrix $\Psi$. Then for every real $d \times q$ matrix $W$ and every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the random vector $WZ + \mu + E$ has law $N(\mu, WW^\top + \Psi)$.

results.title: The probabilistic PCA marginal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Z$ and $E$ be independent random vectors on a probability space, with values in $\mathbb{R}^q$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $Z$ has the standard Gaussian law $N(0, I_q)$ and $E$ has the isotropic law $N(0, \sigma^2 I_d)$ for a real $\sigma^2 \ge 0$. Then for every real $d \times q$ matrix $W$ and every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the random vector $WZ + \mu + E$ has law $N(\mu, WW^\top + \sigma^2 I_d)$.

results.title: Probabilistic PCA covariance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real $d \times q$ matrix $W$ and a real number $\sigma^2$, the probabilistic PCA covariance is the $d \times d$ matrix $W W^\top + \sigma^2 I$.

results.title: The density of the probabilistic PCA observation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $z$ and $\varepsilon$ be independent random vectors on a probability space, with $z$ standard Gaussian in $\mathbb{R}^q$ and $\varepsilon$ Gaussian in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with mean $0$ and covariance $\sigma^2 I$, where $\sigma^2 > 0$. Then for every real $d \times q$ matrix $W$ and every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the law of $x = W z + \mu + \varepsilon$ has density $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, W W^\top + \sigma^2 I)$…

results.title: Sample mean
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For data points $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the sample mean is $\bar x = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^{N} x_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

results.title: Sample covariance
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For data $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with sample mean $\bar{x}$, the sample covariance is the $d \times d$ matrix $S = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^N (x_n - \bar{x})(x_n - \bar{x})^\top$, taken to be $0$ when $N = 0$.

results.title: The log-likelihood of no data is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the empty data set ($N = 0$), the probabilistic PCA log-likelihood at every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$, every real $d \times q$ matrix $W$ and every real number $\sigma^2$ is $0$.

results.title: The mean MLE is the sample mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data with sample mean $\bar{x}$. For every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$, every real $d \times q$ loading matrix $W$ and every real $\sigma^2 > 0$, the probabilistic PCA log-likelihood of the data at $(\mu, W, \sigma^2)$ is at most its value at $(\bar{x}, W, \sigma^2)$.

results.title: The probabilistic PCA likelihood is at most the unconstrained Gaussian maximum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data whose sample covariance $S$ is positive definite, and let $\bar{x}$ be their sample mean. results.title: Probabilistic PCA MLE when the sample covariance has the model form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data with sample mean $\bar{x}$ and sample covariance $S$. If $W_0$ is a real $d \times q$ matrix and $\sigma_0^2 > 0$ is a real number with $S = W_0 W_0^\top + \sigma_0^2 I$, then $(\bar{x}, W_0, \sigma_0^2)$ is a probabilistic PCA maximum-likelihood estimate for the data.

results.title: No latent factors: the noise-variance MLE is the average sample variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data with sample mean $\bar{x}$ and sample covariance $S$, and suppose $\operatorname{tr} S > 0$. Then for every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and every real $\sigma^2 > 0$, the probabilistic PCA log-likelihood of the data with the zero $d \times q$ loading matrix at $(\mu, 0, \sigma^2)$ is at most its value at $(\bar{x}, 0, \operatorname{tr} S / d)$.
